title: Five new multinuclear rare earth complexes: Magnetism and near-infrared luminescence

synthesis.procedure: A mixture of H3L (0.03 mmol) and Nd(dbm)3·2H2O (0.03 mmol) in methanol (20 mL) and acetonitrile (5 mL) was stirred for 6 h at room temperature under atmospheric conditions. The mixture was filtered and the yellow-green filtrate was evaporated slowly in air. After about 10 days, yellow-green strip-shaped crystals suitable for single-crystal diffraction were obtained. H3L was prepared separately by refluxing imidazole-2-carboxaldehyde (10 mmol) and 2-hydroxy-3-methoxybenzoyl hydrazine (10 mmol) in methanol (20 mL) for 5 h at 45 °C, followed by filtration and recrystallization (yield ca. 51%).
synthesis.temperature: room temperature (stirring); ligand synthesis reflux at 45 °C
synthesis.vessel_or_method: open atmosphere; stirring then slow evaporation of the filtrate
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtration; slow evaporation of the yellow-green filtrate under atmospheric conditions gave yellow-green strip crystals

properties.summary: Solid-state NIR excitation and emission show the characteristic Nd(III) f–f bands. Solution UV–vis spectra in dichloromethane show ligand-centered absorptions near 250 and 350 nm. No magnetic data are reported for 1, and the NIR emission was too weak for a decay curve.

properties.summary: Dc susceptibility shows χMT reaching 56.84 cm^3 K mol^-1 at 2 K, with a sharp rise from 18 to 2 K ascribed to intramolecular ferromagnetic interactions. Under a 3000 Oe dc field, frequency-dependent ac signals and peaks demonstrate field-induced SMM behavior; an Orbach fit gives Ueff = 25.3 K and τ0 = 7.21×10^-7 s. Solution UV–vis shows absorptions near 250 and 350 nm. NIR luminescence is not reported for 2.

properties.summary: Solid-state NIR emission of Er(III) spans about 1450–1600 nm with a maximum at 1533 nm (4I13/2→4I15/2). Excitation shows a broad band from about 375 to 475 nm plus peaks near 482 and 525 nm. The emission was too weak for a decay measurement. UV–vis absorptions near 250 and 350 nm are reported. No magnetic data are given for 4.

properties.summary: Solid-state Yb(III) NIR emission (2F5/2→2F7/2) is split into peaks near 990 and 1010 nm. A biexponential decay gives an average lifetime of 1.39 μs, and the quantum yield calculated as τobs/τrad (τrad = 2 ms) is 0.0695%. UV–vis absorptions near 250 and 350 nm are reported. No magnetic data are given for 5.
